chunks: With the first chain of narration, from Ali ibn Mahzyar, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from al-Hasan ibn Abi Sarah, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah Ja‘far ibn Muhammad, peace be upon them both, say:
"A believer does not become a true believer until he is both fearful and hopeful, and he does not become fearful and hopeful until he acts upon what he fears and hopes for."

key_terms.الْمُؤْمِنُ: The believer — one who holds sincere faith (iman) in God
key_terms.خَائِفًا: Fearful — having reverential fear (khawf) of God’s punishment
key_terms.رَاجِيًا: Hopeful — having hope (raja’) in God’s mercy and reward
key_terms.عَامِلًا: One who acts — actively performing deeds that reflect both fear and hope

ai.seo_question: What does Imam Ja‘far al-Sadiq say about fear and hope in faith?
ai.summary: Imam Ja‘far al-Sadiq (AS) defines the essence of true faith as requiring a balance between fear of God’s punishment and hope in His mercy, and emphasizes that this inner state must manifest through action. This teaching was part of the broader ethical discourse in Kufa and Medina, where the Imam’s students sought practical guidance on how internal belief translates into righteous conduct.
word_analysis: and with the chain of narration

en.mulla-asgharali-m-m-jaffer: 27. And with the first chain of narration from ‘Ali ibn Mahzyar, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from al-Husayn ibn Abi Sarah, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah Ja’far ibn Muhammad, peace be upon them both, say:

"A believer does not become a (true and steadfast) Mu’min, till he comes to a situation of being both, fearful as well as hopeful. And that does not occur till he starts performing deeds as one who fears and (also) hopes."
